the BOP exchange and the B3LYP hybrid functional are the most reliable functionals to use in calculating the properties of the second‐ and the third‐row transition metals.
the BOP and B3LYP functionals perform well for second‐ and thirdrow transition metal dimers, but the BOP functional still has some deficiencies for some of the systems.
the BOP functional is a good exchange functional for transition metal dimers, but the correlation functional needs to be improved for transition metal dimens.

the application of the BOP functional to the transition metal dimer systems and with the comparison of the BOP and B3LYP functionals with other density functionals.
the use of density functional theory in the study of the second‐ and the third‐row transition metals.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BOP and B3LYP functionals are the best choices for the calculations on the second‐ and the third‐row transition metals.
the B3LYP hybrid functional is the best among those tested in the second‐ and the third‐row transition‐metal dimers.
the B3LYP hybrid functional is the best choice for the second‐row metal dimer calculations, while the pure BOP exchange functional is not recommended for this purpose.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are still far from the goal of a reliable density functional for transition metal compounds, and the present study suggests that the problem may be more difficult than we thought.

the density functional method is a powerful tool for studying the properties of the transition metal dimers, especially when the combination of the B3LYP exchange‐correlation functional and the basis set of double‐ζ quality is used.
the B3LYP hybrid functional is the most reliable functional for transition metal dimer studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the density functional theory (DFT) is not a universal tool and that it is not possible to find a universal functional that can be applied to all systems.

the B3LYP hybrid density functional performs well in calculating the equilibrium geometries, dissociation energies and harmonic vibrational frequency of the transition metal dimers, and that it can be used to predict the spectroscopic properties of transition metal dimers that are not experimentally available.
the BOP functional is still not suitable for the second‐and third‐row transition metals because of the overestimation of the binding energies.
